extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via Jinja2 fragment concatenation — Remote code execution via Jinja2 sandbox escape, file read, or server compromise [verified: fragment query param concatenated into Jinja2 template string at loan_operations.py:121, Template('Result: ' + fragment).render() allows arbitrary Jinja2 expression injection and sandbox escape.]

OS Command Injection via host parameter in os.system() — Remote code execution on the server as the application user [verified: host query param concatenated directly into os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host) at loan_operations.py:127; _wrk_gate authenticates but does not sanitize, so any token holder achieves RCE.]

Hardcoded Weak Default Session Secret — Full session hijacking and arbitrary user impersonation, including admin privilege escalation [verified: Settings.session_secret defaults to 'dev-only-change-me' (line 28) with no enforcement that the environment variable is set; an attacker who knows this default can forge arbitrary URLSafeSerializer session tokens (line 46 uses signer) and impersonate any user including admins.]

Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read via packet_ref parameter — Arbitrary file read on the server, exposing sensitive data including source code, secrets, and configuration [verified: packet_ref query param used directly as BASE_EXPORT_DIR / packet_ref then read_text() at loan_operations.py:34, allowing path traversal for arbitrary file read.]

Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via url parameter — Internal network reconnaissance, cloud metadata exfiltration, database/Redis access, or port scanning of internal services [verified: url query param passed directly to urllib.request.urlopen(url) at loan_operations.py:43 with no allowlist, enabling SSRF to internal/cloud metadata endpoints.]

Arbitrary Financial State Manipulation via user-controlled amount/state — Direct manipulation of ledger balance and loan state, enabling financial fraud [verified: Arbitrary JSON body at loan_operations.py:52 controls both ledger amount (int(payload.get('amount'))) and state with no integrity checks, enabling balance drain.]

Mass Assignment via user-controlled JSON merged into workset dict — Privilege escalation, unauthorized state changes, and bypass of access controls in the workset [verified: Arbitrary JSON body at loan_operations.py:68 merged into workset dict via workset.update(payload), allowing attacker to overwrite role, tier, approved, and balance fields.]

Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Write via ref parameter — Write arbitrary JSON files outside the intended directory, potentially overwriting application data or configuration [verified: ref query param at loan_operations.py:78 used in BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f'{ref}.json' with write_text; .json suffix does not prevent directory traversal sequences.]

Arbitrary File Write via unsanitized name parameter — Arbitrary file write allowing cron job injection, SSH key overwrite, or application code modification [verified: name query param used directly as file path BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name at loan_operations.py:129 with write_bytes(body), allowing path traversal e.g. ../../etc/cron.d/malicious.]

XML External Entity (XXE) Injection via lxml parser — Local file read (e.g. /etc/passwd, source code), internal network reconnaissance/SSRF, denial of service (Billion Laughs attack) [verified: lxml parser at loan_operations.py:141 configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False, enabling classic XXE for file read, SSRF, and DoS.]

Insecure Session Cookie (secure=False) — Session hijacking via network sniffing on unencrypted HTTP connections [verified: lp_session cookie is set with secure=False on both register (line 425) and login (line 436), transmitting the session token in plaintext over HTTP and enabling session hijacking via passive network sniffing.]

Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via card parameter with |safe filter — Session theft, credential theft, or arbitrary actions performed in the victim's browser context [verified: card query param rendered via Template('{{ card|safe }}') at loan_operations.py:98 with HTMLResponse; |safe filter disables Jinja2 auto-escaping, enabling XSS for any token-holder.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Registration Endpoint — Unlimited account creation enables resource exhaustion (database/disk), spam user profiles, and denial-of-service against legitimate registration. [verified: Registration at main.py:411 has no rate-limiting middleware or decorator anywhere in the codebase, allowing unlimited user creation (database resource exhaustion) and serving as a secondary enumeration vector via 409 vs 200 responses.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Login Endpoint — Password brute-force attacks, credential stuffing, and account takeover [verified: POST /api/auth/login (line 429) has no rate limiting, CAPTCHA, or account lockout mechanism, enabling unlimited brute-force password guessing and credential stuffing attacks.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Password Reset Endpoint — Unlimited password-reset requests enable reset-token brute-force (leading to account takeover) and resource exhaustion through repeated token generation. [verified: Password-reset at main.py:442 also lacks any rate-limiting control — an attacker can enumerate accounts (reset_token null/non-null) and spam the DB with new tokens on each request.]

Account Enumeration via Password Reset Response Body — Attacker can build a list of registered email addresses to target for credential stuffing, phishing, or brute-force attacks. [verified: Password-reset at main.py:452 returns {'reset_token': <token>} for existing emails and {'reset_token': null} for unknown ones, letting an attacker distinguish registered accounts despite the vague message text.]

CSV Formula Injection (CWE-1236) in Admin Export — user-controlled business_name written unescaped to CSV cells — An attacker registers (line 420) with a crafted business_name (e.g. "=HYPERLINK(...)" or "=CMD|...") or a support specialist imports a malicious CSV (line 764). When an admin exports applications (line 783) or decisions (line 787) and opens the CSV in a spreadsheet program, arbitrary formulas execute — exfiltrating data, executing commands, or compromising the admin's host. [verified: User-controlled business_name (from registration line 420 or CSV import line 764) is stored and later written to CSV via csv.writer (line 783) without escaping formula-injection prefixes (=, +, -, @); an admin opening the export in a spreadsheet triggers arbitrary formula execution.]

Open Redirect via unvalidated lane parameter — Phishing attacks: victims trust the application domain but are redirected to attacker-controlled sites [verified: lane param passed to RedirectResponse(lane) at loan_operations.py:62 with no target validation; however _wrk_gate blocks external victims (no token), preventing the classic phishing use case.]

Cookie Injection via user-controlled marker parameter — Cookie manipulation enabling session fixation or downstream logic abuse that trusts the injected cookie [verified: marker query param set as portal_crumb cookie value at loan_operations.py:90 with no validation; cookie name differs from lp_session, so session fixation is not possible, limiting downstream abuse.]

CORS Origin Reflection with Credentials Enabled — Cross-origin data theft and unauthorized state-changing actions from any malicious website visited by an authenticated user [verified: Endpoint at loan_operations.py:116 reflects Origin header into ACAO with ACAC:true, bypassing global CORSMiddleware allow-list; but ops routes authenticate via x-internal-token custom header (not auto-sent cross-origin), limiting practical exploitability.]

Cookie/Header-Based Privilege Escalation via client-controlled badge — Unauthorized access to elevated operational data (payroll, casework) by setting a client-controlled header [verified: Role read from client-controlled ops_badge cookie or x-ops-badge header at loan_operations.py:155; finding itself acknowledges _wrk_gate must be passed first, and token-holders already have full ops access.]

Account Enumeration via Registration Endpoint — An attacker can determine which emails are registered, enabling targeted brute-force or phishing attacks [verified: POST /api/auth/register returns HTTP 409 'Email already registered' for existing emails (line 417) versus different statuses for other validation failures, allowing an attacker to enumerate registered email addresses.]

Password Reset Token Leaked in Response Body — Account takeover of any user whose email is known, including admin accounts [verified: reset_token is returned in the response body to any caller who knows the email (lines 448-451), enabling email enumeration and leaking a sensitive cryptographic value. However, no endpoint in the codebase consumes the token to change a password, so account takeover is not currently achievable.]

Security Headers Explicitly Disabled — Reduced browser XSS protection, increased exploitability of any XSS vulnerabilities in the application [verified: Endpoint at loan_operations.py:125 explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection:0 and CSP:'' on its own response only; other endpoints are unaffected, making this a cosmetic defense-in-depth nit.]
